overview.description: MAZATROL is Mazak's proprietary conversational programming system. Instead of writing G-code line by line, the operator describes the part geometry and operations using units and sequences. MAZATROL auto-generates toolpaths, calculates cutter compensation, and manages tool changes.
overview.key_advantage: Programs directly from a print at the machine without CAD/CAM software. The machine calculates all toolpaths, cutter compensation, and approach/retract moves automatically.
programming_flow: 3. Define workpiece material, dimensions, spindle limit
4. Set finish allowances (X and Z) and work face stock
5. Program units sequentially (coolant, face, turn, drill, bore, thread, groove, mill)
6. Define shape geometry within each unit (linear, taper, convex, concave)
7. Verify with figure check and toolpath simulation
8. Set work shift (Z offset) by touching off

mazatrol_vs_eia.mazatrol: Conversational, auto tip compensation all around tool, auto toolpath generation, shape-based programming
mazatrol_vs_eia.eia_gcode: Traditional G-code, requires manual tip comp direction, more flexible for complex operations, needed for some advanced features
mazatrol_vs_eia.switching: When creating a new program, machine asks 'MAZATROL or EIA' — cannot mix in same program but can call sub-programs

limitations: Cannot calculate radius with angle directly
Does not compensate for drill point angle
No protection against finish before rough in layout

T_Plus.description: Updated MAZATROL controller with improved calculation
improvements: Can calculate radius center position with angle input
Compensates for drill point angle automatically
Better layout protection against crash-causing reordering

features: Material presets with auto speed/feed suggestions
Position page shows part coordinates vs machine coordinates (toggle)
Store button preserves trace display through edits
Cannot edit running program (can create new program while running)
Work number limited to 4 digits without dash
General edge vs general out tool type distinction

work_number.description: Program identifier number, also called workpiece number
work_number.creation: Enter unused work number → machine asks if new → select MAZATROL or EIA
work_number.limit: 4 digits max without dash on some controllers

workpiece_material.description: Material selection that drives auto speed/feed calculations
workpiece_material.note: Material selection primarily affects auto-populated speeds and feeds. Can be overridden.

od_max.description: Maximum outside diameter of workpiece stock
od_max.purpose: Determines rapid clearance height and tool approach distance
od_max.rule: Must be >= actual stock diameter or machine will crash
od_max.tip: Larger values cause more rapid travel time but safer clearance

id_min.description: Minimum inside diameter (0 if solid stock, drill diameter if pre-drilled)

workpiece_length.bar_stock_note: For multiple parts from bar, add all part lengths together plus cutoff kerf allowances

max_spindle_rpm.description: G50 equivalent — maximum spindle RPM for entire program
max_spindle_rpm.note: Only applies to turning spindle. Live tooling RPM is set in tool data.

finish_allowance_x.description: Stock left by roughing tools for finish pass on diameter (radial)

finish_allowance_z.description: Stock left by roughing tools for finish pass on Z axis

stock_removal_workface.description: How much stock to face off the end of the part
stock_removal_workface.note: Set to 0 if part is already faced and Z zero is set to finished surface

END.description: End of program unit — always last in program

parameters.continue: 0 = stop, or specify next work number to chain programs

return_position.tool_change_position: Retracts to safe position based on longest tool in magazine

M_CODE.description: Miscellaneous function unit for coolant, stops, etc.
M_CODE.note: Coolant ON (M8) is typically first unit in 99% of programs

EDGE.description: Facing operation — removes stock from end face of part

parameters.starting_point_z: Distance from Z0 (positive = stock allowance before face)
parameters.final_point_x: Usually 0 (face to center) or ID if tube stock
parameters.finishing_tool: Tool number + offset (can be same as rough)

EDGE.auto_function: Push AUTO button to auto-populate speeds, feeds, and depth from material selection

BAR_OUT.description: OD turning — programs external turning from bar stock

geometry_types.open_geometry: Tool rapids down and feeds across (for stock removal where tool clears at end)
geometry_types.closed_geometry: Tool feeds down into material and feeds across (highlighted icon)

parameters.cutting_point_z: Z start position (usually 0 = face of part)
parameters.depth_of_cut: Radial depth per pass (NOT diameter — diameter changes by 2x this value)

pattern.0: Tool comes up to shoulder then turns up — leaves insert angle relief at shoulder
pattern.1: Tool wraps back to front after reaching shoulder — cleaner shoulders

BAR_OUT.tip: Depth of cut is RADIAL, not diameter. A 0.150 depth changes diameter by 0.300.

BAR_IN.description: ID turning / boring — programs internal turning from pre-drilled hole
BAR_IN.note: Same as BAR OUT but cutting point X is the drill/bore starting diameter
BAR_IN.cutting_point_x: Drill diameter or existing bore diameter

BAR_FACE.description: Alternative facing unit on some controllers
BAR_FACE.note: Similar to EDGE but may have different parameter layout

drill_types.0: Feed in, feed out at same rate (rarely used)
drill_types.1: Peck drilling — feed in, rapid out to start, rapid back, feed more, repeat (chip clearing)
drill_types.2: Peck drilling — feed in, rapid out slightly, break chip (minimal retract)
drill_types.3: Reamer cycle — feed in, feed out at double feed rate

parameters.decremental_depth: Amount subtracted from depth each subsequent peck
parameters.minimum_depth: Minimum peck depth for deep holes (default ~3mm / 0.118 inch)

controller_notes.older_T3: Does NOT compensate for drill point angle — programs to full depth
controller_notes.newer_TPlus: Compensates for drill point angle — drills to major diameter past point

parameters.type: External, internal, face, or back thread
parameters.lead: Thread lead (= pitch for single-start threads). Calculate as 1/TPI.
parameters.angle: Thread angle (60 degrees for standard threads)
parameters.number_of_entrances: Number of thread starts (1 for single-start)
parameters.start_point_z: Thread start position (slightly before actual thread)
parameters.final_point_x: Thread major diameter (same as start for straight thread)

TPC.lead_calculation: For single-start thread: lead = 1 / TPI. Example: 1/4-28 thread → lead = 1/28 = 0.0357

GRV.description: Grooving unit — OD, ID, or face grooves

type_0.use_case: When finish quality on groove walls not critical

type_1.z_reference: Measures from Z0 toward spindle. Width extends toward spindle.

type_2.description: Standard groove with finish and taper capability
type_2.taper: Can create angled groove by offsetting start/finish Z points
type_2.note: Does NOT finish the back wall — only bottom and front. May need additional operation for back wall finish.

type_3.description: Symmetric groove — machines from center outward, finishes both halves
type_3.z_reference: Measures from Z0 to front face
type_3.taper: Supports angled sides with question mark + angle calculation
type_3.advantage: Most versatile — finishes both halves symmetrically

parameters.number_of_grooves: How many evenly-spaced grooves (use pitch for spacing)
parameters.final_point_x: ID at bottom of groove (measured as diameter)
parameters.final_point_z: Z end position (same as start for straight, different for angled)
parameters.chamfer_or_radius: Corner break at top of groove

tool_data.corner_radius: Radius on each side of grooving insert
tool_data.offsets_a_b_c: Different offsets for left, right, and center of grooving tool

GRV.help_menu: Press arrow-over then HELP to see groove type diagrams showing start/finish/width direction
GRV.id_grooves: Same programming as OD but start from inside diameter going outward

parameters.width: Same as tool width for parting
parameters.grooving_tool_offsets: A=left edge, B=right edge, C=center — check Z values in tool data to determine which is which

SUB_PROGRAM.description: Calls a sub-program by work number
SUB_PROGRAM.use_case: Parts catcher activation, complex repeated operations

MANUAL_PROGRAM.description: Allows inserting raw G-code within a MAZATROL program
MANUAL_PROGRAM.use_case: Parts catcher M-codes, special machine functions not available in MAZATROL units
MANUAL_PROGRAM.example: G28 U0 W0 (safe home), M48 (parts catcher activate), M49 (parts catcher retract)

MSS.note: Available on machines with live tooling and C-axis

FACE.description: Face milling operation (for milling flat on face or OD)

shape_patterns.description: Within BAR OUT, BAR IN, and EDGE units, geometry is described using shape patterns

LINEAR.note: Vertical lines (shoulders) are created automatically between horizontal features — only program horizontal lines

parameters.start_corner: Chamfer or radius at start of line (always 45 degrees for chamfer)
parameters.final_corner: Chamfer or radius at end of line

parameters.start_point_x: Starting diameter (or use CONTINUE to auto-fill from previous shape)
parameters.taper_angle: Angle of taper (alternative to specifying both endpoints)

interpolation.question_mark: Enter ? for unknown X or Z value, fill in angle, then press CALCULATE to auto-compute
interpolation.example: Known: start Z=3.0, finish X=2.5, angle=45° → machine calculates finish Z

parameters.final_point_z: Ending Z position (can use ? for unknown)

CONVEX_RADIUS.intersect_position: When using ?, specify Up/Down/Left/Right from center to select correct intersection

CONCAVE_RADIUS.note: Used for fillets, internal curves, relief features

special_features.continue_button: Auto-populates start point X and Z from previous shape's end point
special_features.corner_r_button: Converts any dimension entry from chamfer to radius (toggles R indicator)
special_features.tangent_radius: Place radius value on a TAPER line to create tangent radius between current and next feature — reduces code lines
special_features.shape_end: Signals end of geometry definition for current unit
special_features.figure_check: Graphical preview of programmed geometry (right button → figure check)
special_features.store_button: Preserves current display scale and position through program edits

chamfer_rules.start_corner_always_45: Start corner chamfers are ALWAYS 45 degrees
chamfer_rules.radius_alternative: Press CORNER R button before entering dimension to make it a radius instead
chamfer_rules.chamfer_dimension: Measured in linear Z (or X), NOT across the hypotenuse
chamfer_rules.insert_rollover_trick: Add 0.002 inch to final Z beyond chamfer to ensure insert rolls over cleanly — prevents burr

tool_data_page.description: Defines all tool characteristics for MAZATROL auto-compensation
tool_data_page.access: Left button → Tool Set → Tool Data

fields.nose_radius: Insert tip radius (critical for surface finish calculation and tip comp)

offset_system.geometry_offset: Base position of tool (A dimension = Z length, B dimension = X offset from centerline)

wear_offset.adjustment: Negative X value reduces diameter (e.g., -0.002 takes 2 thou off diameter)
wear_offset.visibility: Wear offset values are visible in geometry display during MAZATROL program run

offset_system.offset_column: Must specify offset column (1 or 2) — leaving at 0 skips wear offset

multiple_offsets.description: Single tool can have offsets A through J (up to 10 orientations)
multiple_offsets.mazatrol_call: Referenced by letter in MAZATROL unit
multiple_offsets.use_case: Different orientations of same tool, different edges of grooving tool

integrex_specifics.a_dimension: Length from spindle gauge face to tool tip (always positive Z direction)
integrex_specifics.b_dimension: Distance from spindle centerline to tool tip (negative for standard OD turning, positive for some orientations)
integrex_specifics.milling_tools: Only length matters (no A/B — tool is on centerline)

orientation.normal: Standard turning orientation, capto key faces back of machine
orientation.flex_tool: Optional — index and clamp every 15 degrees

integrex_specifics.curvic_coupling: Mechanical coupling that clamps spindle for turning operations — transmits force through coupling, not spindle bearings
integrex_specifics.b_axis_clamping: B-axis clamps at every 45-degree increment via its own curvic coupling

tip_compensation.mazatrol_mode: Automatically compensates all around tool based on insert angle, holder angle, and nose radius — no direction needed
tip_compensation.eia_gcode_mode: Requires explicit tip comp direction (1-9) in offset page
tip_compensation.direction_reference: 9 possible directions — relates to which quadrant of insert is cutting
tip_compensation.tip_radius_trick: Increase tip radius value in offset to push tool deeper into radius cuts (opposite of milling cutter comp logic)

auto_function.description: Push AUTO button in any unit to auto-populate speeds, feeds, and depths based on material selection
auto_function.basis: Internal database keyed to material type and operation
auto_function.override: Any auto-populated value can be manually overridden

surface_roughness_numbers.description: MAZATROL uses roughness numbers 1-9 to control finish feed rate
surface_roughness_numbers.calculation: Based on insert nose radius, the machine calculates required feed rate to achieve specified surface finish
surface_roughness_numbers.note: Works better on mills than lathes according to some operators

speeds_feeds_and_cutting_parameters.feed_rate_safety_warning: Be careful not to type 0.120 instead of 0.012 — the machine will NOT catch this mistake and will crash the insert into the part. Double-check decimal placement.

spindle_rpm_limit.description: G50 equivalent set in program header
spindle_rpm_limit.hydraulic_chuck_warning: Centrifugal force reduces hydraulic chuck grip at high RPM — manual chuck does not have this problem
spindle_rpm_limit.live_tooling_rpm: Set in tool data, NOT in program header spindle limit

layout_screen.description: Shows sequence of all operations with tool assignments
layout_screen.rough_priority: Press ROUGH PRIORITY then INPUT to reorder: all rough operations first, then all finish operations
layout_screen.move_process: Manually reorder operations by inserting/moving process numbers
layout_screen.warning: Can accidentally put finish tools before roughing tools and crash — newer controllers protect against this

single_process_rerun.description: Run only one specific process (e.g., finish pass) without running entire program
single_process_rerun.access: Layout screen → Single Process → select process (e.g., 'Finish 3')
single_process_rerun.use_case: Dialing in dimensions after wear offset adjustment — rerun only the finish pass

process_copy.description: Copy a process to create separate rough and finish operations
process_copy.access: Right menu → Process Copy → specify source and destination
process_copy.use_case: Splitting rough and finish tools when rough tool can't reach all geometry (e.g., steep angles on sphere)

figure_check.description: Graphical display of programmed geometry shapes
figure_check.scale: Scale button → enter value (smaller number = more zoom, 0.1 = max zoom on T3)
figure_check.cursor: Arrow keys move white cursor box — becomes screen center on scale change
figure_check.store: Store button saves current scale/position through edits

toolpath_check.description: Full toolpath simulation showing tool motion
toolpath_check.access: Program → Check → Check Continue (full run) or Half Step (step through)

colors.white: Tool nose radius path (offset from part geometry by nose radius)

simulation_screen.description: Full machine simulation with cycle time prediction
simulation_screen.access: Program → Simulation → Simulation Ready → Simulation Start
simulation_screen.accuracy: Predicted time within 3-6 seconds of actual machining time

trace_screen.description: Live display showing tool position during actual machining

procedure: 1. Index to desired tool (usually facing/turning tool)
2. Skim face of part in manual/hand mode
3. Leave Z position where it touched (back X off but keep Z)
4. Go to Program → Program File → select work number
5. Press Z OFFSET → TEACH → enter amount removed (e.g., 0.100 if 100 thou faced off)
6. Press INPUT to set work shift
7. Go to Position → Auto → Work Number → enter program number to verify Z reads correctly
work_shift_and_zero_setting.verification: Z should read the stock removal amount (e.g., 0.100) at the touched-off position
work_shift_and_zero_setting.common_issue: Position display stays on previous program until you manually switch work number in auto mode

integrex_mill_turn_specifics.machine_type: Mazak Integrex — classified as mill-turn machine
integrex_mill_turn_specifics.key_insight: More of a milling machine than turning machine — many users under-utilize milling capability

tool_mounting.capto_taper: Capto tool interface with draw bar clamping
tool_mounting.key_orientation: Key faces back of machine in 'normal' orientation
tool_mounting.manual_clamp: Manual clamp/unclamp available on machine setup page

b_axis.description: Tilting spindle axis for multi-angle operations
b_axis.clearance_benefit: 45-degree orientation provides better chuck jaw clearance for close-to-chuck turning

tool_change.b_axis_must_be_horizontal: B-axis must be at 0 degrees (horizontal) to change tools
tool_change.automatic_orientation: Tool changes automatically orient and clamp for defined setup
tool_change.door_safety: Slower indexing with doors open (safety feature)

hobbing.description: Synchronized milling spindle with C-axis for gear cutting
hobbing.setup: Hob tool in spindle, B-axis at appropriate angle, synchronize rotation

shaping_tools.description: Turning tools used for shaping operations (e.g., square holes)
shaping_tools.method: Define same tool with multiple offsets at different angles (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°)
shaping_tools.execution: Tool change to each offset rotates and clamps at defined angle

programming_tips_and_tribal_knowledge.tip: Always add 0.002 inch beyond the chamfer dimension in Z to ensure the insert nose radius rolls completely over the chamfer. Without this, a tiny burr/sharp edge remains.
When manually overriding feed rates, be extremely careful with decimal placement. Typing 0.120 instead of 0.012 IPR will crash the insert — the machine does NOT catch this mistake.
MAZATROL always programs from the face of the part working toward the chuck. Vertical lines (shoulders) are created automatically — only program horizontal features.
Use the ROUGH PRIORITY button on the layout screen to automatically reorder all roughing operations before finishing operations, reducing tool changes.

When programming a sphere or steep convex radius with a 55-degree diamond rougher, the rougher cannot reach areas steeper than ~30 degrees. Split into separate rough and finish processes — rough with 55-degree, finish with 35-degree diamond using process copy.

On MAZATROL, wear offsets are visible in the geometry display during program run. Some find this annoying but it confirms the wear compensation is active. A negative X wear value reduces the turned diameter.

Using tangent radii (radius button on taper lines) can reduce code from 8 lines to 5-6 lines for complex compound profiles. Method 4 (no CAD) using tangent radii and visual verification is often the fastest approach.
MAZATROL simulation time prediction is remarkably accurate — typically within 3-6 seconds of actual machining time. Use layout screen total time for quoting and scheduling.
Always set offset column to 1 (not 0). Leaving offset at 0 causes the machine to skip wear offset and go by geometry only.
On Integrex machines, MAZATROL always follows the tip of the turning tool — position display automatically updates as B-axis rotates, showing the imaginary sharp corner point of the insert.
The 45-degree B-axis turning orientation on Integrex provides significantly better chuck jaw clearance for close-to-chuck operations, but trades clearance on the tailstock side.

In MAZATROL mode, tip compensation is automatic for all directions. In EIA/G-code mode, you must explicitly set tip comp direction (1-9) in the offset page. MAZATROL defines insert angle, holder angle, and nose radius for full compensation.

Groove types 0 and 2 measure Z from the back side (toward spindle). Type 1 and 3 measure from Z0 outward. Type 3 (symmetric) is the most versatile — it finishes both halves. Types 2 doesn't finish the back wall.

For grooving tools, define offsets A/B/C for left edge, right edge, and center of the tool. Check the Z offset values in tool data to determine which side each offset represents (more negative Z = further from spindle).

For single-start threads, lead equals pitch. Calculate lead as 1/TPI (e.g., 1/4-28 thread: lead = 1/28 = 0.0357). Enter to 4 decimal places. Auto function calculates thread depth and number of passes.

Parts catcher requires a sub-program with manual G-code: M48 to activate, M49 to retract. G28 U0 W0 for safe home position. These M-codes are not in the standard MAZATROL menu — look up in machine manual.
MAZATROL depth of cut is ALWAYS radial (not diameter). A 0.150-inch depth of cut changes the diameter by 0.300 inches. This applies to both turning and milling operations.
Surface roughness number 7 in MAZATROL produces approximately 32 Ra microinch finish, slightly finer. This is the go-to setting for general-purpose finishing with a 0.031-inch nose radius insert.

Setting OD Max larger than necessary causes excessive rapid travel time as the turret retracts to that clearance height on every tool change and approach. Keep it close to actual stock diameter for efficiency.
For bar stock with multiple parts, workpiece length must be the total bar length (all parts plus cutoff kerfs), not individual part length. Otherwise machine will alarm with insufficient material.

When selecting tools in MAZATROL, the tool data window only shows tools capable of the current operation. If a tool doesn't appear, verify its type definition in tool data matches the operation (e.g., general_out for OD turning).

Use the question mark (?) for unknown dimensions in taper programming. Fill in the known dimensions and angle, then press CALCULATE. The machine computes the missing value. This is the fastest way to program chamfers at non-45-degree angles.

On Integrex, tool numbers with letter offsets (T6.01, T6.02, T6.03) correspond to offsets A, B, C. Changing between these in G-code automatically rotates, orients, and clamps the spindle for the defined setup.

To increase groove corner radius cut depth in EIA mode, increase the tip radius value in the offset page (opposite of milling cutter comp where you decrease diameter). Larger tip radius value pushes tool deeper into the corner.

The finish tool will only cut finish allowance amount beyond what the roughing tool left. If the rougher can't reach an area (e.g., steep sphere), the finisher won't clean it up either — must split into separate processes.

error_avoidance.description: Tool ignores wear offset and uses only geometry offset — dimensions won't adjust with wear
Manually reordering layout can place finish operations before roughing — crashes tool into stock
error_avoidance.prevention: Verify rough operations precede finish for each feature when editing layout

error_avoidance.description: 55-degree or wider insert cannot rough geometry steeper than its clearance angle — leaves uncut material
error_avoidance.prevention: Use process copy to split rough/finish; rough with wider angle, finish with sharper tool

error_avoidance.description: Not adding 0.002 inch past chamfer endpoint leaves tiny burr at chamfer edge
error_avoidance.prevention: Always add 0.002 to Z dimension past chamfer for nose radius rollover

error_avoidance.description: Setting workpiece length to single part length instead of total bar length causes alarm
error_avoidance.prevention: Sum all part lengths plus cutoff kerfs for total bar length

error_avoidance.issue: Wrong tool type in tool data
error_avoidance.description: Tool defined as 'general edge' but operation expects 'general out' — tool doesn't appear in selection or simulation fails
error_avoidance.prevention: Verify tool type in tool data matches intended operation

post_processor_implications: MAZATROL programs are NOT G-code — they are stored in proprietary format
EIA/ISO mode on Mazak uses standard G-code with Mazak-specific M-codes
Post processor for Mazak EIA mode should include: G50 spindle limit, CSS/constant RPM modes
Parts catcher M-codes (M48/M49) are machine-specific — include in post processor M-code table
Tool call format for Integrex: T[tool].[offset] (e.g., T6.02 for tool 6 offset B)

relevant_prism_engines.PostProcessorPipelineEngine: Mazak EIA/ISO dialect support — ensure G50, M48/M49, T-code format
relevant_prism_engines.TurningPrintToProgramEngine: MAZATROL-equivalent process planning logic — unit-based decomposition
relevant_prism_engines.SpeedFeedOrchestratorEngine: Auto speed/feed calculation matching MAZATROL's AUTO function
relevant_prism_engines.ToolSelectionEngine: Tool type matching (general_out, general_in, groove, thread, drill)
relevant_prism_engines.ShopToolLibraryEngine: Tool data page equivalent — insert angles, nose radii, holder angles
relevant_prism_engines.ThreadTurningEngine: Threading unit parameters — lead, angle, depth, number of passes
relevant_prism_engines.DrillCycleOptimizationEngine: Peck drilling cycle types matching MAZATROL drill types 0-3
